newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Esec 1996/97 sales rise, but profit drops.
newsitem.headline: Esec 1996/97 sales rise, but profit drops.

text.p: Esec Holding SA said group sales in the 1996/97 financial year to end February, rose to 325 million Swiss francs from 215 million, but group profit is not expected to reach the previous year's 26 million.

Esec, which makes assembly machines and assembly lines for the semiconductor industry, said in a statement profit would be down because it was sticking to its decision to hold research and development spending at the budgeted figure of some 50 million francs, a budget based on expected 1996/97 sales of 440 million francs one year ago.

"Consolidated sales fell short of original expectations, which had still been estimated at 380 to 400 million after the first nine months," Esec said, noting the strong contraction in the semiconductor market worldwide, especially in the second half of 1996.
Orders at hand at the end of February were some 115 million francs adn for the current year Esec expects further growth of 40 ot 50 percent.
Sales are still expected to exceed one billion francs by year 2000, Esec added.
Further information of Esec's 1996/97 accounts will be provided mid-May.
The decline led to a 16 percent fall in capital investments for automatic semiconductor assembly machines as compared with the previous year.

"Although the margin on operational business was slightly improved through careful management of resources, the consolidated profit will still not equal the previous year's figures of 26 million francs," Esec said.

Esec also said that it would propose a "shareholder-friendly solution" to the annual meeting in connection with depreciation of goodwill from the acuisition of Zevatech, a U.S. silicon packaging group that was acquired last July.
Esec also said its biggest single order was booked in March for over 100 wire bonders. The order was taken by Esec Korea.
